questions.question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down until it passes.
Turn on your flashers.
Pull to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, you must pull to the side of the road and stop.

questions.question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, you should:

options.text: Pull next to them and yell.
Stay calm and let it go.
Flash your high beams.
Cut them off in return.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and let it go.
questions.explanation: Do not take road rage seriously. If another driver cuts you off, stay calm and keep driving safely.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, what should you do?

options.text: Stop immediately.
Help any injured people.
Call the police.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle right away. If needed, move it out of traffic. Call the police and request an ambulance if necessary. Help stop any bad bleeding with direct pressure. Wait for emergency help to arrive.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You may use this lane.
No traffic is allowed in this lane.
You have the right-of-way.
You must merge into this lane.

questions.explanation: A green arrow pointing down over a lane means you may use that lane.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving in bad weather?

options.text: A sudden weather change means you should change how you drive.
Slow down when driving in rain and fog.
Watch for vehicles coming up behind you in bad weather.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When weather changes suddenly, adjust how you drive. Always slow down in rain or fog. Watch for vehicles behind you that may be going too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: Which statement is true about seat belts and child restraints?

options.text: Never put an infant in the front seat of a car with airbags.
Airbags can harm an infant or small child, even in a minor crash.
Make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Before driving, always wear your seat belt and make sure all passengers do too. Seat belts greatly reduce the chance of injury or death in a crash. Children 12 and under should sit in the back seat in a proper restraint. Never put a rear-facing infant seat in the front seat if there is a front airbag.

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Eating, drinking, or smoking.
Talking or texting on a phone.
Changing the radio or CD.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Drivers must focus fully on driving. Any extra task, even small ones, can be a dangerous distraction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No passing zone.
Winding road.
Pedestrian crossing.
Low ground railroad crossing.

questions.explanation: This sign warns of a low ground railroad crossing. Railroad tracks cross the road at a steep slope. The bottom of low vehicles may drag or get stuck on the tracks.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your driving skills and judgment?

options.text: It helps driving skills but harms judgment.
It harms both driving skills and judgment.
It does not affect driving skills or judgment.
It does not affect judgment but harms driving skills.

questions.correctAnswerText: It harms both driving skills and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reactions and makes it hard to see clearly. It also hurts your judgment about speed and distance, makes you more reckless, and increases risky behavior.

questions.question: When should you not pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a hill or curve.
When a school bus has flashing lights.
When approaching an intersection.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Never pass if an oncoming car is in the passing lane, if a curve or hill blocks your view, at an intersection, before or on a railroad crossing or bridge, or in any no passing zone. Do not pass a stopped school bus with flashing red lights unless you are on the other side of a divided highway with a median or center turn lane.

questions.question: Which of the following increases a driver's crash risk due to distraction?

options.text: CD player
Radio
Cell phone
All of the above

questions.explanation: Using a cell phone, radio, or CD player while driving is dangerous. These distractions take your attention away from the road and increase your crash risk.

questions.question: What causes "highway hypnosis"?

options.text: Staring at the roadway for long periods of time.
Taking frequent rest stops.
Getting too much sleep before your trip.
Driving short trips on expressways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Staring at the roadway for long periods of time.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead at the road for too long and stop checking ahead, behind, and around your vehicle. You zone out and may crash into traffic slowing or stopping ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Turn right after making a complete stop.
Right turns are not permitted.
Left turns are permitted.
None of the above.

questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign. It tells drivers that right turns are not allowed at this location.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, what should you do?

options.text: Stop your vehicle at or near the scene.
Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle at or near the accident scene. Move it out of traffic if possible. Stay out of traffic lanes—another vehicle could hit you. Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on an interstate?

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.
Always use cruise control.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
Change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes or passing. Only stop on the shoulder in an emergency. Change lanes as infrequently as possible. Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic or poor weather.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, what should you do?

options.text: Go to the next exit.
Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.
Flag down a police officer for help.

questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, continue to the next one. Do not stop, back up, swerve across lanes, or cross the median. These actions are illegal and very dangerous.

questions.question: What is the purpose of highway markings?

options.text: They are usually not important.
They are only found in construction zones.
They provide information for drivers.
They are usually red and blue in color.

questions.explanation: Highway markings provide information to drivers. They help you position your vehicle correctly, show safe passing zones, and warn about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What should you do when making a left turn?

options.text: Proceed quickly because you have the right-of-way.
Expect pedestrians to yield to you.
You have the right-of-way if the traffic signal is a flashing red light.
Yield to oncoming traffic that is close enough to cause a collision.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to oncoming traffic that is close enough to cause a collision.
questions.explanation: Always yield to other drivers and pedestrians when making a left turn. Yield to oncoming traffic unless a sign, signal, flagger, or officer tells you otherwise.

questions.question: When are seat belts most effective?

options.text: Only the driver needs to wear one.
Passengers should wear them on long drives.
All occupants should wear them on expressways.
All occupants should wear them every time the car is driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: All occupants should wear them every time the car is driven.
questions.explanation: Everyone in your vehicle should wear a seat belt at all times. In a crash, an unbelted person becomes a flying object and can injure others in the vehicle.

questions.question: How much lane space are motorcycles entitled to?

options.text: The bicycle lane.
The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.
The width of the sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are entitled to the same full lane width as all other vehicles. This is important for the safety of the motorcycle rider.

questions.question: Turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes, leaving a curb, or merging into traffic is:

options.text: A bad driving habit.
A good driving habit.
Unnecessary.
Not necessary if you use the rearview mirror.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder before changing lanes. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for bicycles.
Bicycles not allowed.
Bicycle repair shop ahead.
Bicycles have the right-of-way.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that bicycles may be in the area ahead.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Get some coffee.
Open your window.
Stop driving.
Turn on the radio.

questions.explanation: Driving while tired is as dangerous as driving under the influence of alcohol. Stop driving if you feel tired.

questions.question: When you see a steady red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Drive through if there is no other traffic.
Continue driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.explanation: A red traffic light means you must come to a complete stop. Running a red light is illegal and dangerous. You may turn right on red if there is no sign prohibiting it.

questions.question: Alcohol causes:

options.text: Loss of concentration.
Poor coordination.
Slower judgment.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Even small amounts of alcohol hurt your vision, judgment, concentration, and coordination.

questions.question: Drivers must yield to pedestrians:

options.text: Only if the pedestrian is a child, elderly, or blind.
Only if the driver is not in a hurry.
Only at night.
When the pedestrian is in a crosswalk at an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the pedestrian is in a crosswalk at an intersection.
questions.explanation: Slow down or stop at intersections to let pedestrians cross in marked or unmarked crosswalks. Watch for pedestrians who may suddenly cross in front of you.

questions.question: What happens if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

options.text: The medicine reduces the effect of alcohol.
Alcohol helps the medicine cure a cold.
The combination can multiply the effects of both.
There is no effect because they are different.

questions.correctAnswerText: The combination can multiply the effects of both.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with medicine can increase the harmful effects of both. For example, one drink combined with cold medicine can affect you like multiple drinks would alone.

questions.question: If a train is close or moving fast enough to be dangerous, you must:

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Wait until the train completely passes before crossing.
Cross the tracks at your own risk.
Find another route across the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the train completely passes before crossing.
questions.explanation: Look and listen for trains before crossing railroad tracks. If a train is near or moving fast enough to be dangerous, do not cross. This applies even if there are no signals or the signals are broken.

questions.question: If a police officer stops you, you should:

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.
Get your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.
Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
Get out of your car and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the wheel and ask passengers to keep their hands visible. Stay in your vehicle unless the officer tells you to get out. Wait for the officer to ask for your driver license, registration, and insurance.

questions.question: When driving on major highways, you should:

options.text: Stay alert.
Keep your eyes moving.
Be ready to react to hazards.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stay alert on highways and be ready for unexpected hazards. Keep your eyes moving and do not stare at one thing for more than a few seconds to avoid highway hypnosis.
